caveat: Outlook is an analytical assessment as of October 2026, not a forecast. 2025 figures are IMF estimates/projections.
data_source: IMF World Economic Outlook via DataMapper (latest vintage, accessed October 2026)
debt_management: Nigeria's debt was negligible after the 2005 Paris Club deal: 5.2% of GDP in 2008, the series low. The 2014 oil crash ended the era of oil-financed budgets, and the government borrowed steadily to fund deficits: debt reached 39.3% of GDP in 2024, the series high, easing to a projected 36.3% in 2025. The ratio flatters the problem: with revenues among the world's lowest as a share of GDP, debt service consumes an enormous share of government income, and much borrowing has been expensive domestic debt. The 2023 reforms (subsidy removal, naira float) improved the fiscal arithmetic, but sustainability depends on raising non-oil revenues, which has eluded every government.
inflation_management: Nigeria's inflation has been structurally high and is now in crisis territory. It averaged 8-13% from 2006 to 2015 under a managed naira, then the 2016 devaluation pushed it to 15.7-16.5% in 2016-17. The central bank's multiple-exchange-rate regime and deficit financing kept it at 11-19% through 2022. The 2023 reforms were the breaking point: subsidy removal and the June 2023 naira float sent inflation to 24.7% in 2023 and a series high of 33.2% in 2024, with 23.0% projected for 2025. The central bank has hiked rates aggressively, but with food inflation far higher than headline and the naira still adjusting, expectations remain unanchored. There is no formal inflation target; policy is crisis management.

key_events.event: Oil price crash: GDP in USD terms peaked at $811.1bn (2014), then collapsed; 2016 recession.
Muhammadu Buhari won the presidency, ending 16 years of PDP rule.
COVID-19 and oil crash; #EndSARS protests shook the country.
Naira redesign fiasco ahead of elections; Bola Tinubu won the disputed 2023 vote.
May 29, 2023: Tinubu removed the fuel subsidy; June 2023: naira floated and FX rates unified; inflation surged to 33.2% in 2024.
Dangote refinery began operations, promising to end fuel imports.

outlook_next_decade: The base case is painful adjustment: if the 2023 reforms hold, inflation should fall to single digits and growth recover on refining and gas; if they are reversed, the crisis resumes. Upside is large (Dangote refinery, tax reform, oil production recovery); downside is political: reforms have made Tinubu deeply unpopular and the 2027 election looms. Uncertainty is high: Nigeria has started reforms many times, but never finished them.
